CONFOUNDERS: The trial was large (N=3451) and adequately powered. The failure mode is most consistent with 'wrong_population' — bevacizumab works in metastatic colorectal cancer but the adjuvant setting (post-surgery, micrometastatic disease) may not have the same angiogenesis dependency. The biology of established metastatic disease (where bevacizumab has proven benefit) differs from the adjuvant micrometastatic setting. The AE profile shows some increase in serious diarrhea in XELOX+Bv (5.46% vs 2.49% control) and some vascular events, but these are not at a level that would constitute dose-limiting toxicity preventing adequate dosing — the trial completed with full enrollment and follow-up. The primary failure is that bevacizumab added to adjuvant chemotherapy did not improve DFS and may have numerically worsened outcomes, suggesting the anti-angiogenic mechanism does not translate to benefit in the adjuvant colon cancer setting.
